discovery: Experimental discovery of CP violation in the B-meson system at asymmetric B factories

nominees.name: Fumihiko Takasaki
nominees.affiliation: High Energy Accelerator Research Organization (KEK), Japan

subfield: Experimental particle physics (flavor physics / CP violation)
motivation: In 2001 the BaBar and Belle experiments, at the asymmetric-energy B factories PEP-II and KEKB, observed large time-dependent CP violation in B0 -> J/psi K_S decays. This was the first CP violation seen outside the kaon system. Measuring sin2beta with high precision confirmed that the Kobayashi-Maskawa phase is the dominant source of CP violation in the quark sector, and so provided the experimental basis for the 2008 Nobel Prize in theory. It required a new experimental concept: boosted B pairs, precision silicon vertexing that resolves picosecond decay-time differences, flavor tagging, and very high luminosity. These experiments turned flavor physics into a precision test of the Standard Model and set the template for Belle II and LHCb. Hitlin (founding BaBar spokesperson), Takasaki (Belle and KEKB leadership) and Olsen (Belle co-spokesperson) were central in conceiving, building and leading these experiments.
